inputs.text: A country has a duty to enforce its immigration laws; that is not the problem here. The problem is a government that cannot give clear, lawful direction to the officials charged with carrying them out. If prosecutors now say the May memo authorized no arrests, then ICE needs rules it can rely on—not shifting interpretations that leave officers exposed and public confidence damaged. Legal proceedings must be orderly and honest, but so must immigration enforcement. Confusion at the top serves neither the rule of law nor the people expected to uphold it.
